condition: Acute myocardial infarction presenting as epigastric pain
summary: 68-year-old diabetic woman with 3 hours of epigastric "indigestion", nausea and sweating; ex-smoker, hypertensive. No chest pain words. ESC 2023: ECG within 10 minutes and hs-troponin before any GI label.

inputs.hpi: Three hours of heavy upper abdominal discomfort like bad indigestion, with nausea and sweating; came on while hanging out washing. Antacid did not help. Feels weak. Type 2 diabetes for 15 years, high blood pressure, ex-smoker.

exam.general: Pale and sweaty. Pulse 98/min, BP 150/88, SpO₂ 96%.
exam.abdomen: Soft, minimal epigastric tenderness, no guarding.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute myocardial infarction (inferior)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Epigastric pain with sweating in a diabetic woman — acute coronary syndrome until ECG and troponin exclude it.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE has no cardiac disease; top 3 cholecystitis, peptic ulcer, GORD.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an ACS "must-not-miss" node or a cross-check prompt for epigastric pain + diaphoresis + cardiovascular risk (diabetes, age, smoking).

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Symptom inference needs the chip "chest pain"; with epigastric pain + nausea it ranks GORD, pancreatitis, perforated ulcer.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected ACS in an outpatient setting: emergency services/ED.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Same-day call only (score 33): CHEST_PAIN_TERMS and the cardiac red flag need the words "chest pain/crushing/left arm/jaw"; epigastric pain with sweating in a diabetic scores age and comorbidity only.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: rules.ts: add an atypical-ACS rule (epigastric pain/indigestion + sweating/diaphoresis, or + diabetes/age ≥50) → urgent with "ECG now".

mustAlarm.knownGapNote: Safety prompts fired are "Appendicitis — emergency surgical indication" (from "Acute abdominal pain" CC) and "Acute abdominal presentation"; nothing cardiac.

mustInclude.proposedFix: As level-emergency; chest-pain/ACS prompt with ECG + troponin.

mustExclude.note: A dyspepsia plan without cardiac exclusion is the failure mode.

guideline.name: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
guideline.section: Suspected ACS: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact; hs-troponin 0 h/1 h (or 0 h/2 h) algorithm; atypical presentations (epigastric pain, nausea, diaphoresis) are more common in women, older people and people with diabetes
guideline.citation: Byrne RA, Rossello X, Coughlan JJ, et al. Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3720–3826.

rationale: Dangerous mimic: an inferior MI in a diabetic woman described only as indigestion. Keyword engines that need the words "chest pain" will route her to dyspepsia; the guideline response is an immediate ECG and troponin.

authoring.author: Claude (upper-GI cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations written from the guideline texts, not yet checked against the source (verified: false).
